strings.name: Narendra Modi
strings.role: Prime Minister of India · Governance and international diplomacy
strings.summary: Modi moved from BJP organisational work to leading Gujarat, then became India’s prime minister in 2014 and began a third term in 2024. His governments pursued infrastructure, financial inclusion and tax reform while expanding international diplomacy. His leadership has also faced controversy over religious relations and civil rights. The BJP lost its individual parliamentary majority in 2024, making coalition support necessary.
strings.coverageNote: Research cutoff: 13 November 2026; selected milestones span 1950–2026. An official profile updated in November 2026 confirms his role. Controversies and judicial findings are distinguished; government self-assessments are not independent evidence of results.
strings.facts.fact-01.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.fact-02.label: Early career
strings.facts.fact-02.value: BJP organisational work; chief minister of Gujarat, 2001–2014
strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: National policy changes
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: His governments pursued financial inclusion and the Swachh Bharat sanitation programme, and introduced the Goods and Services Tax in 2017.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Sustained leadership and diplomacy
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: Has led India’s government since 2014 and participated in multilateral diplomacy; began a coalition-supported third term in 2024.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Opens India AI Impact Summit
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Presented human-centred and inclusive AI-governance proposals at the New Delhi summit.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Begins third term
strings.timeline.event-02.text: After the BJP fell short of a majority, the National Democratic Alliance supported the formation of his government.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Supreme Court dismisses appeal
strings.timeline.event-03.text: The court rejected an appeal against the Special Investigation Team’s clearance of Modi and others, which found insufficient evidence for prosecution.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Begins second term
strings.timeline.event-04.text: Took the oath again after the BJP won a parliamentary majority.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Introduces Goods and Services Tax
strings.timeline.event-05.text: His government implemented a nationwide GST, changing India’s indirect-tax system.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: First becomes prime minister
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Took office after leading the BJP to an election victory, moving from state to national government.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Gujarat riots prompt controversy
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Serious communal violence occurred during his chief ministership. His government’s response faced lasting criticism; see the 2022 entry for the legal outcome.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Becomes Gujarat chief minister
strings.timeline.event-08.text: Began leading the state government and remained in office until 2014.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Born in Vadnagar
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Born in Gujarat; later joined organisational work with the RSS and BJP.
strings.influence.rationale: His sustained leadership of India and digital-infrastructure, industrial and diplomatic policies have broad influence on the Global South and the international economy.
